summary: A hexagonal iron screwpile light off the north end of Kent Island, lit in 1872 and dismantled in 1964; a small flashing light and fog bell stand on its foundation.

lens.note: Fifth order, fixed white, from 15 November 1875 (Board report for 1876, via LighthouseFriends). The USLHS record says fifth order installed in 1872.

structures.note: Hexagonal iron screwpile foundation; the house was dismantled in 1964 and the foundation now carries a small flashing light and fog bell.

access.note: USLHS record: not open to the public.

events.note: Hexagonal iron screwpile light off the north end of Kent Island, at a cost of $15,000 (Chesapeake Chapter).
Ice in winter 1872-73: two ice-breaker piles carried away, two main columns broken; the light was discontinued for a time.
Riprap protection added under an appropriation of $5,000.
Light changed on 15 November 1875 from a three-and-a-half-order flashing red to a fifth-order fixed white lens (Board report for 1876). The USLHS record gives a fifth-order lens in 1872.
Ice banked against the platform in January without damage; 100 cubic yards of stone added to the riprap.
Some 954 feet of new decking laid; soundings taken around the light.
Tender Jessamine and assistant keeper William M. Midgett rescued an oysterman who had fallen overboard near the light (20 November 1916, per the 1927 Bulletin).
Keeper Arthur Midgett assisted the occupants of a disabled motor boat near the station (September).
Keeper Arthur Midgett assisted a disabled motor boat with three men aboard (5 July).
House dismantled; an automatic light erected on the iron screwpile foundation, which now carries a small flashing light and fog bell.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The USLHS record gives a fifth-order lens installed in 1872. The Board's report for 1876 (transcribed on LighthouseFriends) says the light was reduced from a three-and-a-half-order flashing red to a fifth-order fixed white on 15 November 1875. The story follows the Board report.
The structure is gone as a house (dismantled 1964), but the iron screwpile foundation stands and carries a small light, so both 'lost' and 'standing' describe parts of the site.

notes_for_editor: The Board's reports for 1870 to 1899 are not in the local corpus (the corpus begins with the 1891 volume). The station chronology before 1891 comes from LighthouseFriends' transcriptions of the reports; each footnote names the report year. The transcriptions should be checked against the printed reports before publication. Disagreements in the sources: the site's distance from Love Point is about one mile in the 1871 transcription and about one and a quarter miles in the 1872 transcription; the 1870 plan says a little over a mile from the north end of Kent Island. The lens: fifth order in 1872 (USLHS) against a three-and-a-half-order original (Board report for 1876). The Commissioner's 1919 'Love Point Shoal Light Station' is matched by name only. The USLHS roster has 84 lines; C. C. Dowdy and two USCG lines are open-ended ('at least' or no end year). The roster's head keepers are used as printed. In the 1899 and 1901 Board reports the name is OCR-damaged ('Lave Pointy' in 1899, 'Cliester' in 1901); the quotes used are clear of the damage. The William M. Midgett line in the 1916 Bulletin is damaged by OCR; the quote used is the clear part of the sentence. The USCG Historian's page for Love Point could not be read (the Wayback capture returned no text). Cheslights says the light was 'demolished in the 1960s'; LighthouseFriends and the USLHS record say dismantled in 1964. Wikipedia was not used. No newspaper search produced a usable hit for Love Point (one search with the word 'light' returned unrelated pages). Accessed dates use the system date, 2026-10-28. Checker notes (2026-10-27): The Board's 1899 and 1901 volumes are in the corpus and were checked on the scan pages cited (1899 entry 595, scan page 143; 1901 entry, scan page 148). The 1870 to 1876 Board entries rest on LighthouseFriends' transcriptions, which were checked against the cited report years inside that transcription. The 1926 and 1927 Bulletin entries and the Index to the 1924-1929 Bulletin were checked on the PDF pages cited; the Midgett index line is on PDF page 20, not 18. The Commissioner's ironwork entry (scan page 452) sits in the 'Repairing and rebuilding aids to navigation, Atlantic Coast' section whose amounts run to June 30, 1919, so it is labelled as the fiscal year ended 30 June 1919; identification with this light rests on the name 'Love Point Shoal' and LighthouseFriends' 1919 entry. The 1916 Bulletin rescue was read on the page image (PDF page 50). The 1927 Bulletin (PDF page 22) names Captain Manyon among his commendations, including 20 November 1916.
